editorial:
Ever wonder what actually happens behind the closed doors of those massive banks you see downtown? You get a front-row seat to that world here, following Jérôme Kerviel. He starts as a regular guy who just wants to prove himself, but he quickly turns into a trading superstar. The vibe is a mix of high-stakes pressure and corporate greed, showing you how easy it is to get carried away when you are making millions of dollars in seconds. It feels like a race against time as you watch him climb the ladder while hiding a massive secret from his bosses.

What really works is how the movie makes complex money talk easy to understand. The acting is solid, and the tension builds up perfectly as the 2008 financial crash starts to hit. While some parts of the middle can feel a bit slow, the payoff is worth it. You should definitely check this out if you like stories about people who play a dangerous game and lose. For the best experience, try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video or renting it on Apple TV to see all the detail in those fancy office settings.
endingExplained: Everything crashes down when the bank discovers the billions in fake trades Jerome made. Instead of admitting they let it happen, the bank makes him the sole villain to save their own reputation. You see him get arrested and face the law while the executives stay rich. It ends on a sad note, showing that in the world of big money, the little guy always gets thrown under the bus to protect the company.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves true stories about money and corporate scandals.
